:JUDGMENT:

: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments are briefly stated as under:
That on 30.08.2024 at about 12.00 p.m. Lingaiah was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LH-1049 near KPTCL Station, in between Tataguppe - Bijjahalli,

Kodihalli Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time, a driver of Mahindra Bolero Goods SCCH 5 Carrier bearing Reg. No.KA-11-C-6695 being driven by its driver at very high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against said Vijayamma vs Pavan C on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98005489/
2
Lingaiah, due to the impact of the same, Lingaiah sustained severe injuries and succumbed to fatal injuries on spot.

Immediately after the accident, body was shifted to General Hospital, Kanakapura, wherein post mortem was conducted and handed over the dead body to the petitioners, who shifted to their residence and conducted funeral and obsequies ceremonies by incurring expenses of Rs.3,00,000/- including transportation, charges etc.,
3.
At the time of accident, deceased/Lingaiah was aged about 59 years, doing fishery work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 to 4 are daughters of the deceased.
Due to sudden and sad demised of the deceased, petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering.
With SCCH 5 regard to accident, Kodihalli Police have registered a case in their crime No.122/2024 for the offences punishable under Sec.106, 281 of BNS.
Respondent No.1 is owner, respondent No.2 is insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the court through counsel and filed written statement.
In written statement respondent No.1 denied averments of the petition with regard to occurrence of the accident, death of the deceased Lingaiah, age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Further submitted that, Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier bearing Reg.
No.KA-11-C-6695 was insured with respondent No.2 vide its policy No.331300432669/ 000/00 and the policy is valid from 30.03.2024 to 29.03.2025 and driver of the said offending vehicle was SCCH 5 having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-C-6695 appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement and stated that, it is the insurer of the said vehicle and its liability to indemnify respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it seeks protection under Sec.147 and 150 of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, driver of the said offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied relationship of petitioners with the deceased.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH 5 6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties this court framed following issues:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Lingaiah, S/o. Late.

Chikkaiahdaiah died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 30.08.2024 at about 12.00 p.m.
near KPTCL Station in between Tataguppe -  Bijjahalli, Kodihalli Hobali,
Vijayamma vs Pavan C on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98005489/
3  Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District due to rash and negligent driving of Bolero Goods Carrier Vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-11-C-6695 dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1/ wife of the deceased is examined as PW-1 and marked SCCH 5 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.
My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 :

In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased has examined as PW-1.
In the chief-examination affidavit she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of driver of Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier, PW-1 got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of crime detail report as Ex.P.3,
copy of sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of SCCH 5 IMV Report as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest report as Ex.P.6,
copy of P.M.Report as Ex.P.7, copy of mahazar as Ex.P.8. copy of Sec.133 notice as Ex.P.9 and copy of reply as Ex.P.10.
10.

Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.

In the absence of iota of evidence, it can be held that death of Lingaiah was due to road traffic accident occurred on 30.08.2024 at about 12.00 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LH-1049 near KPTCL Station, in between Tataguppe - Bijjahalli, Kodihalli Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District.
11. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, the very accident is occurred due to negligence of SCCH 5 the driver of the Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No.KA-11-C-6695.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence of petitioners this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

4 12.
Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Lingaiah was aged about 59 years as on the date of accident.
For proof of age of the deceased, copy of aadhar card of the deceased is marked as per Ex.P.12,
wherein the year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1965, the alleged accident was occurred on 30.08.2024.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 the age of the deceased is considered about 60 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 9 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla SCCH 5 Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was doing fishery work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In order to prove the said fact, petitioners have not produced any income proof documents.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.16,500/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 14. Further petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are daughters of the deceased Lingaiah.
To prove the said fact, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card of petitioner No.1 to 4 which are marked as Ex.P.12 reveals SCCH 5 that, they are the legal representatives of deceased Lingaiah.

15. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6, then 1/4 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 10% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged in between 50 to 60 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.18,150/- p.m. hence, which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 10% with reference to his age.
SCCH 5 17.
Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

the monthly income as (+)1,650/-

5 deducted towards personal Rs.4,538/- = and living expenses

Monthly income Rs.13,612/-p.m (iii) Compensation after Rs.13,612 x 12 x 9 multiplier of 9 is applied Total Rs.14,70,096/-
18.

As per judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi, in Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014, the loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be enhanced at the rate of 10 percent in every three SCCH 5 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore the petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is for Rs.48,000/- towards consortium and petitioner No.2 to 4 being daughters of the deceased is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards filial consortium.

Further they are also entitled for Rs.18,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.18,000/-
towards funeral expenses.

19. The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 14,70,096-00 2. Loss of consortium 96,000-00 3.
Loss of Estate 18,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 18,000-00 Total 16,02,096-00 20.
Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,02,096/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 21.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.331300432669/000/00 which is valid for the period from 30.03.2024 to 29.03.2025, the alleged accident was occurred on 30.08.2024 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

6

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,02,096-00/- (Rupees sixteen lakhs two thousand ninety six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 70:10:10:10 in the award amount.

The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH 5 Draw award accordingly.
